chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the man when he intends to cleanse himself (istinja), with which of the two should he begin, the back part or the front part? So he said: With the back part, then with the front part.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: To cleanse oneself after relieving oneself (istinja)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for cleaning the body after urination or defecation according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of istinja by establishing a specific sequence: cleaning the primary area (al-maq'dah, typically the anus) before the secondary area (al-i'llah, typically the penis or urethra). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on thoroughness and order in ritual purity (taharah), ensuring that the most significant impurity is addressed first to maintain hygiene and spiritual cleanliness.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Al Sabaty, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked about the man when he intends to cleanse himself, with which of the two should he begin with, the back part or the front?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With the back part, then with the front part’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabatiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
Should a man after using the toilet first wash his buttocks or his urethra?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is buttocks, then urethra.’”
